item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Tehran Fires Missile Barrage at Israel After U.S. Claims Progress on Talks
item.summary: Israeli officials said missiles launched from Iran had hit Tel Aviv and other parts of the country. President Trump said there had been “very strong talks” with Iran to end the war, though Iranian officials did not confirm that.

item.title: Trump Sours on Keir Starmer Over UK’s Decision Not to Join Attacks on Iran
item.summary: President Trump once called Prime Minister Keir Starmer a friend. But Britain’s decision not to join the attacks on Iran has led to merciless mocking by the president.

item.title: How North Korea’s Kim Jong-un Is Using the Iran War to Justify His Nuclear Arsenal
item.summary: He delivered a lengthy speech at his country’s rubber-stamp Parliament, declaring that his nuclear power will shield his country from American hostility.

item.title: Take Shorter Showers: South Korea Kicks Off an Energy-Saving Drive
item.summary: President Lee Jae Myung called on the public to cooperate, likening the energy supply disruption caused by the Iran war to the Asian financial crisis and the pandemic.

item.title: Sidelined by War With Iran, Gaza Residents Remain in Limbo
item.summary: The new war has led to panic buying and a surge in food prices for Gazans as they try to recover from Israel’s two-year offensive against Hamas.

item.title: Caught Between Two Conflicts, Afghans Flee Iran
item.summary: The war in Iran is choking off Afghanistan’s main economic lifeline and has forced at least 70,000 Afghan workers and students there back home to a nation embroiled in another conflict.

item.title: Trump Delays Threat to Iran, but War Negotiations Are in Early Stage
item.summary: President Trump postponed his threat to strike power plants in Iran, citing “productive conversations” with the Iranians. But officials said the talks were in an early stage and not substantive.

item.title: ‘Strong Talks’ With Iran?
item.summary: President Trump’s latest statements about discussions with Iran don’t necessarily signal an end in sight to the war, but they do buy him some time.

item.title: Here’s What Happened in the War in the Middle East on Monday
item.summary: Conflicting signals about whether any negotiations to end the fighting were in progress created confusion.

item.title: Government Cuts Gut the Memory of Argentina’s Dirty War
item.summary: Fifty years after the military dictatorship, Argentina’s government is defunding human rights groups and promoting a revisionist account of the junta’s crimes.
